assigned_slot.public_class: flash-next-class local endpoint (the class of rounds 15, 17, 19 and 21)
assigned_slot.state_when_the_round_began: generation-hung: model-list endpoint answered in 0.03 s while chat completions timed out at 180 s and at 90 s; a 256-token completion eventually returned in 115.2 s (about 0.3 tokens per second)
assigned_slot.action: rotated to the pool's next generation-healthy slot, per the runner's documented pool rotation (a model-list hit alone is not health)

serving_slot.public_class: 27B-class local endpoint (the class rounds 16 and 18 measured)
health_detail: one 2048-token health attempt refused with http_502 after 66.1 s (upstream gateway limit on this deployment); this attempt is what motivated disclosure 2 below and it spent no grid prompt
two short capacity diagnostics of 16 and 38 completion tokens (13.0 s and 1.2 s) used to decide whether the slot could carry a 36-cell grid
one health probe inside the probe run, ok in 52.0 s at 38 completion tokens under the 256-token health budget
one further health probe during the gate-hash-guarded resume, ok in 1.3 s
serving_slot.cross_round_identity: no endpoint identity fingerprint is archived (public-only rule), so the claim that this is the same deployment as rounds 16 and 18 is a slot inference, not a verified fact

post_hoc_or_pre_dispatch_patches.what: health-probe output budget lowered from the operating budget (2048) to a dedicated 256-token health budget
post_hoc_or_pre_dispatch_patches.why: a 2048-token health call was killed by an upstream gateway at about 66 s on this deployment while a 256-token call returned in about 1 s; the health probe's job is to prove generation health, not to spend the operating budget

post_hoc_or_pre_dispatch_patches.when: after all 36 cells were archived, during aggregation
post_hoc_or_pre_dispatch_patches.what: aggregate() P2a and P2b lines patched to read the trichotomy status from the classification rows instead of the per-level token rows (KeyError: 'status')
post_hoc_or_pre_dispatch_patches.why: the status field lives in the classification output, not in the token rows; the port read the wrong table
post_hoc_or_pre_dispatch_patches.recovery_path: gate-hash-guarded --resume plus --analyze at the final HEAD; --selftest re-run green (355 checks) after the patch; gate.json rewritten by --gate under the same gate hash

call_accounting.note: no cell hit the 2048-token ceiling: every one of the 36 attempts ended with finish_reason stop, maximum completion 1958 tokens

timing.note: summary.json reports wall_seconds 0.0 and an empty phase1_walls because it was regenerated by --resume, which spent no grid prompt; the numbers above come from the per-attempt timestamps in raw.jsonl and from the local run log

estimate_corrections.why: the two-phase estimator divides MAX_TOKENS by the phase-1 wall, so a short answer at a low wall is a rate upper bound, not a throughput; on the original dispatch the phase-1 walls of 24.7 s and 22.4 s at 304 and 391 completion tokens are about 13 tokens per second single-stream
estimate_corrections.consequence: the concurrency choice is conservative (1); the grid still finished in 1129 s

estimate_corrections.why: the character-proportional position estimate is approximate and is recomputed from the archived attempt fields inside aggregate() at analysis time, per the round-21 lesson that estimates stored at dispatch time rot; raw.jsonl is never rewritten
estimate_corrections.consequence: budget_replay_content_only in summary.json is the recomputed ladder (7/20/30/36 of 36 at 256/512/1024/2048)

lesson_for_the_runner: exit status and dispatch-time health are not the round record: this round would have died at the health probe with no artifact had the pool not carried a second generation-healthy slot. A pre-dispatch generation probe with a real token budget, and a re-probe of the assigned slot at run time rather than at queue time, are the runner-side fixes.
